correctness.rationale: The irreducible Fourier decomposition has two scalar blocks and (p-1)/2 two-dimensional blocks; determinant D is symmetric in inversion and sparse in cyclic differences. Prime full-spark bounds D roots when nonzero; two-term U excludes rank-zero 2D blocks when determinant vanishes identically. The support partitions k=1,2,3,4 exhaust all cases, and explicit 1/2/3/4-tap witnesses attain 2p,p,2p-4,p-1. Five exact cyclotomic and modular example tests agree. Infinite conclusion uses the proved prime Fourier-minor theorem, not the finite tests.

value.rationale: Exact minimum image dimensions for k=1..4 naturally quantify sparse convolution compressibility. The structural k=2-to-3 upward jump is p-4, unbounded as p grows, and k=4 shows a sharp rank collapse due to a two-coset factorization. The nonabelian Fourier block argument explains why this exact-support phenomenon survives despite two-dimensional irreducibles; the result answers a full natural first-window classification rather than an arbitrary fixed-size calculation.
